note: The demo page's summary and next steps, written once by the agent loop from the page's own figures and replayed for the same simulated account.
summary: This is a simulated account, so results are scored against the simulation's truth, not real sales. Over 8 weeks, the agent's weekly budget moves produced 39.6 conversions a day against 37.3 with budgets left alone. That is +6.1% at the same total budget, and it captured 86% of the available gain. TabPFN raised 4 alerts on unusual days and 3 were real problems. The ±50% day-over-day rule raised 24 alerts and 22 were false alarms. Next, move budget toward Retargeting and investigate the flagged days.

recommendations.action: Raise the daily budget from 182.96 USD to the recommended 228.70 USD, an increase of 45.74 USD (25.0%). Submit it as a proposal for approval, funded by the cuts below so the total stays at 2313.94 USD.
recommendations.evidence: Retargeting is limited by budget and is the only campaign expected to gain. Expected conversions rise from 4.01 to 4.75 a day, about 0.74 more. The 8-week trial of this approach gained 6.1% at the same total budget.
recommendations.expected_effect: About 0.74 more conversions a day from Retargeting. This is a model estimate, so the real gain may differ.
recommendations.measurement: Compare Retargeting conversions a day and total account conversions a day against the trial level of 39.6 over the next few weeks. Watch Retargeting spend for spikes, since one was flagged there on 2026-08-05.
recommendations.reversal: Set the Retargeting budget back to 182.96 USD through a new proposal, and restore the funding campaigns to their current budgets.

recommendations.target: Brand Search and Non-Brand Search daily budgets
recommendations.action: Lower Brand Search from 42.43 USD to 31.82 USD (-10.61 USD) and Non-Brand Search from 487.65 USD to 455.78 USD (-31.87 USD). Leave Shopping almost flat, from 1600.90 USD to 1,597.64 USD. Submit these as proposals together with the Retargeting increase.
recommendations.evidence: The result recommends these shifts at no change in total budget. Expected conversions fall by 0.46 a day for Non-Brand Search (8.54 to 8.08) and by 0.12 for Brand Search (1.02 to 0.90). Together that is 0.58 a day lost. Shopping is expected to lose 0.05 a day.
recommendations.expected_effect: The expected net gain across all four campaigns is small, about 0.11 conversions a day. The Retargeting gain only slightly outweighs the losses elsewhere, so the benefit depends on the model being right.
recommendations.measurement: Track conversions a day for each campaign over the next few weeks and compare them with the expected values above. Confirm the account total does not fall below the current level.
recommendations.reversal: Restore Brand Search to 42.43 USD and Non-Brand Search to 487.65 USD through a new proposal if account conversions drop.

recommendations.target: Unusual days: Shopping tracking, Retargeting spend, Brand Search conversions
recommendations.action: Check the Shopping conversion tracking for 2026-07-30. Check the Retargeting spend settings and change history for 2026-08-05. Review the Brand Search conversion surge on 2026-08-01 to confirm it was genuine. Keep the TabPFN 95% expected range as the alert method, and stop relying on the ±50% day-over-day rule.
recommendations.evidence: On 2026-07-30 Shopping recorded 6.0 conversions against an expected 22.33, which was a real tracking outage. On 2026-08-05 Retargeting spent 300.59 USD against an expected 169.61 USD, a real spend spike. On 2026-08-01 Brand Search recorded 6.0 conversions against an expected 0.99, a real conversion surge. The 2026-08-02 Shopping flag (14.0 against 27.24 expected) was a false alarm, so treat it as lower priority. On a real account, flags prompt an investigation and are not findings.
recommendations.expected_effect: Catching tracking outages and spend spikes early protects the conversion data the budget moves depend on.
recommendations.measurement: Count alerts and confirmed problems each week. TabPFN had 1 false alarm among 4 alerts, against 22 among 24 for the ±50% rule.
recommendations.reversal: Alert method changes are reversible. If TabPFN misses real problems, bring back the ±50% rule alongside it.
